# Semantic cache measurement — v1

Generated by `make cache-eval` from the data in this directory; the definitions, criterion
and verdict rule are fixed in `preregistration.md` (with its amendments). Point estimates
only; no confidence intervals (declared). Every lookup goes through the gateway's own
`SemanticCacheService` over an in-memory Qdrant.

## Verdict (pre-registered)

Production embedding `nomic-embed-text` (digest `0a109f422b47`). Criterion: precision >= 0.95 on both (a) PAWS-X and (c) the paraphrase replay; a grid point counts only with >= 20 hits in each set; tier rule off: every original is stored at its router tier and looked up with min_tier_rank=0, so every entry (rank 0, 1 or 2) is eligible.

**no safe threshold on the grid**: no eligible t reaches 0.95 on both sets. Recommended t = **0.99**, the eligible t with the highest min(precision_a, precision_c), which does not meet 0.95; the product default for new tenants becomes 0.99.

| t | eligible | (a) hits | (a) precision | (a) recall | (c) hits | (c) correct | (c) precision | (c) recall |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0.90 | yes | 1805 | 0.453 | 0.901 | 173 | 139 | 0.803 | 0.803 |
| 0.99 | yes | 245 | 0.620 | 0.168 | 25 | 23 | 0.920 | 0.133 |

(c) counts 173 valid paraphrases (of 200 registered) and the 1000 originals leave-one-out; a hit of a leave-one-out original is always a false hit.

In (a), 907 of 1999 pairs are paraphrases (0.454), and (a)'s precision stays between 0.451 and 0.620 over the grid: PAWS-X pairs are adversarial word swaps of the same words, which this embedding scores as near-identical whether or not the meaning changed.

## Saving vs repetition rate

A trace of 1000 requests per rate r (seed 20261022), served in order through a gateway cache that starts empty, tier rule on. Exactly round(r × 1000) requests, at seeded positions, nested across rates (the repeats of a lower rate are among those of a higher one), repeat a prompt asked earlier: half exact repeats (same text and vector), half its valid paraphrase. The other requests are new Spanish corpus prompts, each at most once (at r = 0 every one of the 1000 is sent once). A first version of the trace drew each request's repeat independently; with this seed that gave 61 repeats at r = 0.037 (a rate the trace no longer uses) instead of 37, so the count is now fixed and the rate on the axis is the rate in the trace. A miss is served at the request's router tier (target 0.95) at the cost captured for that prompt and tier (`src/nebula/data/router_replay_v1.json`; local = 0) and stored; a hit costs 0. A correct hit keeps the quality of the cached answer's tier for that prompt (`benchmarks/ground-truth/v1/tiers.jsonl`); a false hit is worth 0. Costs in USD per 1000 requests.

### Consistency with the router's cited cost

- The shipped router at target 0.95 on the whole corpus (1250 prompts) costs USD 1.706 per 1000; the thesis cites the nested estimate, USD 1.701 (difference +0.0055, within 0.01: the shipped weights are refit on all data, the nested estimate routes each fold with weights and thresholds chosen without it).
- The trace serves only the Spanish prompts, which cost more to route: the shipped router costs USD 1.848 per 1000 on them (the nested estimate for Spanish is USD 1.824). At r = 0 the trace's router-only cost equals it exactly (checked when the report is built).
- At r = 0 the cache still serves some requests: distinct prompts close enough to an earlier one are false hits (t = 0.90: false hits 17, cost 1.820, t = 0.99: false hits 1, cost 1.846).

## Sensitivity: `nomic-embed-text-v2-moe` (does not enter the verdict)

The same rule applied to this model would give **no safe threshold on the grid**: no eligible t reaches 0.95 on both sets. Recommended t = **0.98**, the eligible t with the highest min(precision_a, precision_c), which does not meet 0.95. It changes nothing in the product.

| t | eligible | (a) hits | (a) precision | (a) recall | (c) hits | (c) correct | (c) precision | (c) recall |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0.90 | yes | 1541 | 0.466 | 0.792 | 146 | 139 | 0.952 | 0.803 |
| 0.98 | yes | 357 | 0.594 | 0.234 | 48 | 44 | 0.917 | 0.254 |

## Limitations

- **The validity rule has a known blind spot.** It keeps any rewrite whose length is 0.5 to 2.0 times the original's, so it cannot see what a rewrite says. An automated review (an AI code-review agent, not a human rater) read about 75 of the valid paraphrases and flagged 4 that answer the prompt instead of rewriting it, 1 corrupted with CJK characters, and 2 code prompts whose rewrite renamed the identifier the test asserts on; these counts are not a human check. They stay in (c) because the rule was fixed before the rewrites were seen and is not changed after. Such a rewrite that misses its original lowers the replay's recall; one that still matches its original counts as a correct hit although the cached answer may not serve it. The 40-pair human check measures how faithful the set is.
- **Router tiers are in-sample.** The shipped router's weights were fit on these prompts' labels, so the router-only quality in the savings table is optimistic for the Spanish set; the cache's effect is read as the change from that baseline, not as an absolute quality.
- A paraphrase is priced at its original's captured cost on the same tier, and is assumed to need the same answer (the human check tests that assumption).
- A hit on a different corpus prompt is a false hit with quality 0, even when the two prompts are near-identical (the MBPP pair `es:code-0113` / `es:code-0138`, disclosed in the pre-registration).
- One tenant, single-turn requests, entries never expire within a trace: the cache's context key and TTL never block a hit here.
- Scores are Qdrant's (single-precision vectors); PAWS-X uses the committed cosines.
- `nomic-embed-text` is an English model; the multilingual model is reported as sensitivity.

Git commit checked out at generation: `0ff7602440c6d317b4fd943bbc61f9c15c3ec270`; these inputs differed from it when the report was generated: `scripts/cache_eval/replay.py`. The SHA-256 of each file in report.json is the authority (`provenance.files`, with the untracked corpus vectors too), and `provenance.vectors` hashes the vectors used.
